sections.label: Unvaccinated workplace ban date
sections.summary: From 15 January, unvaccinated workers cannot return to their workplace even with a negative test.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With effect from 15 January, the unvaccinated will not be allowed to go back to their workplace even if they tested negative.

sections.label: Justification for workplace ban
sections.summary: A question asks what justifies preventing unvaccinated people from returning to their workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is the justification for preventing the unvaccinated from returning to their workplace?

sections.label: Unvaccinated bear decision consequences
sections.summary: The unvaccinated bear the brunt of their decision, and the Government is concerned about 52,000 unvaccinated employees' health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They bear the brunt of their decision not to be vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government is concerned about the health of the 52,000 unvaccinated employees.

sections.label: 52,000 unvaccinated employees revealed
sections.summary: The Government has revealed that there are 52,000 unvaccinated employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has revealed that there are 52,000 unvaccinated employees.

sections.label: ICU rates among unvaccinated
sections.summary: MOH statistics from 1 May to 15 December 2021 show ICU case percentages among unvaccinated by age group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MOH's COVID-19 statistics from 1 May to 15 December 2021 showed that, amongst the unvaccinated, the percentage of COVID-19 cases requiring ICU ranged from 0.051% to 0.53% for those aged 20 to 49, 2.4% for those aged 50 to 59 and 7.2% for those aged 60 to 69.

sections.label: Rescind unvaccinated workplace ban
sections.summary: The speaker sees no basis to fear ICU overwhelm and urges rescinding the 15 January ban, keeping testing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I would be happy to receive more accurate figures from MOH.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, based on what I currently see, there does not appear to be any basis to fear that allowing the unvaccinated to return to the workplace would overwhelm our ICU facilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We urge the Government to rescind the ban on the unvaccinated returning to their workplace from 15 January and continue with the current arrangement of using testing as the means to control the spread of COVID-19.

sections.label: VDS on children commitment
sections.summary: A question asks whether the Government can commit to not imposing VDS on children for at least another year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In light of the fact that COVID-19 is milder in children, can the Government commit to not imposing VDS on children for at least another year to give parents more time to digest new information, monitor developments and perhaps wait for more vaccination options to become available?

sections.label: VDS reopening and hospitalisation risk
sections.summary: VDS enables safe reopening while minimising hospitalisation risk, as non-fully vaccinated persons are more likely to become critically ill or die.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Our experience over the past few months shows that VDS will enable us to continue our path of safe and calibrated reopening whilst, at the same time, minimising the risk of hospitalisation to preserve healthcare capacity, in particular, limited hospital and ICU resources.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: It is important to note that non-fully vaccinated persons who are infected with COVID-19 are more than seven times more likely to become critically ill in ICU, compared to those who are fully vaccinated – 0.5% of cases versus 0.07% – and 12 times – 1.7% of cases versus 0.14% – more likely to die.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Among seniors aged 60 and above, the incidence of fully vaccinated and non-fully vaccinated cases who are critically ill in the ICU are 1.9 and 35.9 per 100,000 population respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The incidences of fully vaccinated and non-fully vaccinated seniors who died are 0.3 and 8.2 per 100,000 population respectively.

sections.label: Daily cases and ICU beds
sections.summary: Cases were sustained at 3,000 per day, with 100 to 170 serious cases occupying ICU beds each day.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The number of cases was sustained at 3,000 per day, as mentioned by Minister Ong Ye Kung earlier, and, the serious cases, who had to be seen in hospitals, resulted in 100 to 170 cases occupying ICU beds each day.

sections.label: Omicron surge and vaccination coverage
sections.summary: Another Omicron surge is expected, but vaccination coverage has improved to 87% completing full regimen and 89% receiving at least one dose.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We now face a prospect of another surge of cases due to the Omicron variant.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We are in a better position than before, as our vaccination coverage has improved greatly over the past few months to 87% of our entire population completing their full regimen, with 89% receiving at least one dose.

sections.label: Adjustments to VDS policies
sections.summary: VDS adjustments remove the negative PET concession for unvaccinated individuals and reduce the recovered persons exemption period from 270 to 180 days.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Further adjustments to our VDS policies have thus been made to ready us for these potential increases in cases as well as to allow us to better understand the nature of the Omicron variant and its differences from the Delta variant.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: These include the removal of the concession for unvaccinated individuals to produce a negative Pre-Event Test (PET) result prior to participating in a VDS event or activity and the reduction of the exemption period for recovered persons to enter VDS settings from 270 days to 180 days.

sections.label: Unvaccinated workers workplace return
sections.summary: From 15 January 2022, unvaccinated workers, except those medically ineligible, cannot return to the workplace even with a negative PET result.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To strengthen our protection against a large wave of cases locally and to keep our workplace safe, the MTF announced that, from 15 January 2022, unvaccinated workers, barring those medically ineligible, will not be able to return to the workplace even with a negative PET result.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: As of 2 January 2022, there were about 48,000 employees who had not taken any vaccine dose.

sections.label: COVID bills, subsidies, children vaccination
sections.summary: Subsidies and MediShield Life can cut eligible Singaporeans' COVID bills to about $2,000 to $4,000, and there are no plans to extend VDS to those aged 12 and below.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: While the median bill size for COVID-positive patients receiving treatment in acute hospitals who require both ICU care and COVID-19 therapeutics is estimated to be about $25,000, access to means-tested Government subsidies and MediShield Life coverage can reduce the bill to about $2,000 to $4,000 for eligible Singaporeans in subsidised wards.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: With regard to extending VDS to children in the community, public, preschool and school settings, there are, presently, no plans to do so for those aged 12 and below.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The focus at this time is to ensure our children are well-protected as we begin vaccination for those aged five to 11, using the paediatric doses of the Pfizer/BioNTech/Comirnaty COVID-19 vaccine.

sections.label: Immunity, VDS, ICU statistics, job loss
sections.summary: Vaccination, boosters and VDS have been integral to the COVID-19 response, and the two-thirds ICU statistics cannot be applied to the current small number of unvaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In summary, increasing population immunity through vaccinations and boosters, reinforced with VDS, has been integral to our COVID-19 response in protecting the vulnerable and ensuring that our healthcare system can cope with the incoming Omicron wave, as well as any future infection waves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: We have got just a few minutes for clarification, Ms Hazel Poa.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: I have explained earlier in my speech why we cannot apply the two-thirds ICU statistics to the current situation because of the changing vaccination rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Therefore, it is not reasonable to apply those statistics to the current small number of unvaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: So, I presume that in implementing this strong measure which risks 48,000 livelihoods, MOH must have done studies on what is the impact, specifically on the number of expected job loss versus the additional burden on the hospital ICU utilisation.

sections.label: Unvaccinated workers taxing ICU capacity
sections.summary: Even 1% of the 48,000 currently unvaccinated workers is a high number that would tax ICU bed capacity and scarce resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: One, I think even if you are looking at 48,000 of the workers that are now currently unvaccinated and just talking about 1% of them, that is already a high number and that is already going to tax our ICU bed capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We are actually just looking at how, even with that small number, it is going to impact and tap on scarce resources which could very well be deployed for other needs within the community.
